index_title: Real closure, harmless owners and original correspondence coordinates
scope: Preparation for OTHER Lean projects. General exact algebraicity projection/finite closed preimages, harmless full invariant owner parameters, original normalized correspondence coordinates and internally proved finite-action avoidance. No maximal-core safe descent, rooted construction or EPPA is imported.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Abstract avoidance/full quotient intervals, source closure, normalized correspondence and palette-conditional concentration have distinct premises.

assumptions.name: Current actual source
assumptions.statement: M is a nonempty countable transitive homogeneous source in a FINITE complete symmetric binary language with semantic homomorphic CCO and equality-inclusive RAW orbitals. Countability is retained from the packaged joint-lifting provider. No SAP or EPPA is assumed.

assumptions.name: Infinite-source branch
assumptions.statement: For correspondence coordinates and harmless-owner criteria M is infinite. Finite-class packets F may be nonidentity and NONEXACT. The quotient projection and full-preimage closure lemmas do not need the infinite-source restriction.

assumptions.name: Finite-exact normalization only where required
assumptions.statement: The actual source has no nonidentity invariant finite-class FULL RAW EXACT equivalence. This is used for finite-exact intersection, correspondence gluing and original canonical coordinates, not the general harmless-owner or quotient-closure branches.

assumptions.name: Complete minimal-direction list
assumptions.statement: E_1,...,E_r enumerate ALL distinct inclusion-minimal infinite invariant equivalences of the current original source. They are exact by the prepared minimal-cut provider. Canonical multi-coordinate conclusions require r>=2; no arbitrary subset may replace this complete list.

assumptions.name: Strong closed safe palette
assumptions.statement: S is a set of ORIGINAL diversity atom names with strong amalgamation of finite ABSOLUTELY real-acl-closed induced spans, with each new off-base cross edge in S. Used only by unsafe concentration and its clique consequence, not structural correspondence, closure or harmless-owner criteria.

assumptions.name: Finite common kernel family
assumptions.statement: There is a finite indexed family of equivalences K_i on the original carrier with common kernel K=meet_i K_i having finite real classes. For the algebraicity/source claims they are actual FULL RAW EXACT invariant equivalences of M; the pure finite-fibre cardinality argument uses only the stated kernel property. No compatible-tuple or onto finite projection hypothesis is supplied.

assumptions.name: Absolutely closed finite quotient targets
assumptions.statement: Each D_i is finite and ABSOLUTELY acl-closed in the actual quotient M/K_i. Full inverse images are intersected in M. For the rectangle instance C meet K=Id and both actual coordinate targets project onto the same finite nonempty owner B; B itself need not be acl-closed.

assumptions.name: Abstract action and finite moving request
assumptions.statement: For the generic avoidance result G is any group acting on a set, A and Z are finite, and EVERY a in A has infinite G-orbit. Empty A/Z and nonfaithful actions are allowed. No topology, model theory or source geometry is needed.

assumptions.name: Real finite-orbit algebraicity
assumptions.statement: Use real acl as finite orbits of the full pointwise automorphism stabilizer; owner classes are actual quotient imaginaries fixed individually. In the current countable homogeneous finite language, finite real bases have finite acl. Monotonicity, finite-base idempotence and transitivity follow from stabilizer finite-index arguments recalled in N00, not an extra constructional provider.

assumptions.name: Generic commuting equivalence lattice for unary transfer
assumptions.statement: For C19 only, a transitive action has a finite lattice of commuting invariant equivalences and a greatest finite-class F; F has a UNIQUE least strict coarsening D. All relevant relative indices are uniform. No exactness, normalization, CCO, countability or safe palette is assumed in this bridge.

assumptions.name: Generic canonical quotient language
assumptions.statement: For C35 only, G acts transitively on a nonempty set, K is G-invariant, and the quotient language names ALL actual old-G pair orbitals. The full automorphism group of this named quotient may be larger than the G image. No global surjectivity or group section is assumed.

imports.name: RAW exact products and nonempty meets
imports.statement: Reuse exact RAW multiplication and nonempty meet-product distribution, including identity words, and symmetry-based original commutation. No STRONG/NR2 step.

imports.name: One original automorphism for a finite joint map
imports.statement: Every finite genuine joint real/exact-sort partial isomorphism extends to ONE original automorphism. Retain the current countability premise; no global quotient automorphism section.

imports.name: Nested mixed pair colours
imports.statement: For real/actual exact owner, the mixed pair orbital depends only on the projected owner pair, including quotient diagonals. This validates fixed-real/moving-owner and moving-real/fixed-owner finite requests.

imports.name: Actual quotient standing-source inheritance
imports.statement: Every actual exact quotient retains the standing source in its complete old-group canonical orbital language. Full quotient invariant transport is C35. Strict diversity-rank decrease is proved locally in C10/C16 by counting orbital blocks; it is not attributed to an unexported rank clause of this provider.

imports.name: Canonical original real hull
imports.statement: For x outside finite nonempty real A, x is algebraic iff the actual intersection of Gamma(col(x,a)) classes through a is finite; Gamma is the FULL generated invariant equivalence, not necessarily exact. Empty parameters are treated separately.

imports.name: Singleton and one-direction real closure
imports.statement: Reuse specifically C11: acl(a)=F[a] and, for an infinite actual source with ONE minimal infinite invariant direction, acl(A)=F[A] for every finite real A. This does NOT imply harmlessness of named owner imaginaries.

imports.name: Packets, cores and finite-index calculus
imports.statement: Reuse elementary finite-index Sigma/F construction, monotone canonical kappa cores, finite [R:kappa(R)], Sigma(kappa(R))=Sigma(R), and actual word exactness of every core including empty-word Id. No exactness or distributivity of F is inferred.

imports.name: Relative index transposition
imports.statement: Reuse C02 finite towers, restriction inequalities and [A join B:B]=[A:A meet B] for commuting invariant equivalences; do not rely on cardinal division for infinite classes.

imports.name: Actual minimal infinite cuts are exact
imports.statement: Every inclusion-minimal infinite invariant equivalence is its nontrivial exact packet core, with no proper infinite refinement. Keep the FULL invariant lattice separate from its exact sublattice.

imports.name: Finite-square regularizer in a normalized source
imports.statement: Reuse ONLY finite_packets C19/C22: the stabilized product of all F-atom squares is a finite-class exact H0 containing every such square. Current normalization forces H0=Id, hence every F atom has square Id. No thin-bottom conclusion is inferred from a theorem that merely assumes thinness.

imports.name: Actual finite-family set CRT
imports.statement: Use only the two-coordinate commuting-equivalence realization for a full rectangle with C meet K=Id. General finite-kernel closure pullback below does not require compatible tuple surjectivity.

imports.name: Actual exact lattice for rectangle realization
imports.statement: The actual exact equivalences form a commuting distributive lattice, discharging I11 for the rectangle. The FULL invariant lattice is not asserted distributive.

imports.name: Actual same-sort mixed orbital identity
imports.statement: For original exact C,K and old atom a, C;a;K=(C join K);a;(C join K). This is separate from rectangle closure and no global group section is asserted.

definitions.name: Full finite packet and generated equivalence
definitions.statement: F=Sigma(Id) is the greatest finite-class invariant equivalence, possibly nonexact. Gamma(a) is generated by the actual symmetric orbital a.

definitions.name: Finite-exact normalized support
definitions.statement: No nonidentity FULL RAW exact invariant equivalence has finite classes; this does not force F=Id.

definitions.name: Global correspondence cut
definitions.statement: For a GIVEN NONIDENTITY actual exact invariant EQUIVALENCE E, R_E is the union of ALL actual RAW atoms a, including equality, for which E meet a squared=Id. It is defined on the whole original carrier.

definitions.name: Original nonmaximal packet cores
definitions.statement: For the complete E_i list set R_i=R_(E_i) and C_i=kappa(R_i). These symbols are NOT redefined by later maximal pseudocomplements hat C_i.

definitions.name: Strong closed unsafe clique
definitions.statement: An unsafe clique is a finite set all of whose DISTINCT pairs have old atom outside S. Strong closed amalgamation is an input about absolutely closed spans, not arbitrary finite SAP.

definitions.name: Full inverse-image intersection
definitions.statement: W=intersection_i pi_(K_i)^(-1)(D_i); its joint quotient-map fibres are K-classes. No independent coordinate surjectivity is assumed.

definitions.name: Harmless actual owner classes
definitions.statement: A full invariant owner kernel H is harmless if adding any finite collection of its actual classes as imaginary parameters does not change real acl over any finite real A. Mixed finite owner sorts are included.

definitions.name: Bad neighbour colour for one minimal direction
definitions.statement: For a chosen infinite minimal E, p is bad if E meet p squared subset F. In one E-class its p-neighbours of x lie in a single finite F-class.

definitions.name: Canonical tuple closure target
definitions.statement: For finite real A and exact K_i with finite common kernel, membership in real acl(A) is equivalent to every quotient coordinate being algebraic over its projected input.

definitions.name: Virtual containment preorder
definitions.statement: For subgroups U,V of a group, U preceq V iff [U:U meet V] is finite. Mutual virtual containment is commensurability; choose maximal CLASSES in this finite preorder.

definitions.name: Finite transporter obstruction
definitions.statement: For a group action request (a,z), {g:g(a)=z} is empty or one LEFT coset of the point stabilizer. Infinite a-orbit means that stabilizer has infinite index.

claims.name: Virtual containment is a preorder
claims.statement: Restriction of finite subgroup indices and the tower formula prove transitivity of preceq; mutual preceq is an equivalence relation. In a finite list of subgroup types, its quotient preorder has a maximal class.

claims.name: Finite coset-cover theorem proved internally
claims.statement: A group cannot be covered by finitely many left cosets of infinite-index subgroups. Induct on distinct subgroup types: choose a maximal preceq class H, enlarge all commensurable-type cosets to finitely many H cosets, choose a disjoint further H coset, and intersect the remaining cover to cover H by fewer infinite-index subgroup types. No external Neumann theorem is assumed.

claims.name: One motion avoids every finite forbidden pair
claims.statement: Each nonempty transporter is a left coset of an infinite-index stabilizer by A08. C02 prevents their finite union from covering G, so choose one g outside; it moves the entire finite A away from Z. Empty requests use identity.

claims.name: Exact reflexive finite support is identity after normalization
claims.statement: For an actual FULL RAW exact invariant EQUIVALENCE E and a nonempty symmetric actual atom a, ASSUME D=E meet a squared is contained in F. D is exact and reflexive by I01. Its increasing positive powers stabilize to an exact equivalence inside F; A03 forces that stable equivalence and hence D to be Id.

claims.name: The global cut contains identity and all finite packets
claims.statement: R_E is invariant/reflexive/symmetric. Every thin F atom squares to Id by I10, so F subset R_E, with no exactness assertion about F.

claims.name: Only finite thin E edges belong to the cut
claims.statement: If a subset E is an R_E atom then a squared subset E and E meet a squared=Id imply a squared=Id. It is a thin involution and belongs to F. Thus E meet R_E=E meet F.

claims.name: Each cut colour is functional into a fixed E class
claims.statement: If a subset R_E, two a-neighbours of the same point lying in one E-class are E meet a squared-related and hence equal. Include the equality-atom case.

claims.name: The finite real and fixed-owner request is genuine
claims.statement: For actual x a y b z and x prime E x with col(x prime,z)=col(x,z), the map x->x prime,z->z fixing all E-classes of x,y,z is a finite partial isomorphism in the actual joint language by I03. Degenerate x=z gives the identity target automatically; no inconsistent noninjective request is formed.

claims.name: Joint exact lifting makes the global cut transitive
claims.statement: Lift C08 by I02. Fixed z and fixed E[y] plus b-functionality force g(y)=y; a-functionality then forces g(x)=x. Thus each outer colour c in a;b is functional in every E-class, equivalently E meet c squared=Id, so R_E is an equivalence.

claims.name: Structural gluing dichotomy without EPPA
claims.statement: If R_E is finite-class, greatest F gives R_E=F. Otherwise C=kappa(R_E) is infinite nonidentity exact with finite [R_E:C]. E meet C is exact finite-class, hence Id by normalization. Actual nonidentity quotient inheritance gives strict diversity-rank decrease for M/E and M/C.

claims.name: Two-anchor algebraicity test
claims.statement: If x E_i u but not x F u, then Gamma(col(x,u))=E_i by minimality. I05 gives x in acl(u,v) iff x R_i v: the forward finite meet is reduced to Id by C04; the reverse defines x uniquely in E_i[u] intersect col(x,v)[v]. Treat x=v directly.

claims.name: Different minimal directions lie in opposite correspondences
claims.statement: For i!=j, E_i meet E_j is exact finite-class and hence Id. Each atom inside E_j squares inside E_j and thus lies in R_i. Consequently E_j<=R_i and E_i<=R_j.

claims.name: An unsafe pair cannot evade both correspondences
claims.statement: For an unsafe x,y outside R_i,R_j choose u in E_i[x] outside F[x] and v in E_j[y] outside F[y]. C11 places both x,y outside acl(u,v). Strongly S-amalgamate their closed extensions over that base. Preserved fine spokes plus RAW meet-product distribution force the new cross edge to have its LITERAL old unsafe atom, contradiction.

claims.name: Two-equivalence rook lemma and exceptional cliques
claims.statement: If every pair of a finite set is related by one of two equivalences, the whole set lies in one equivalence class of one of them. Apply C13 to every pair of minimal-direction indices: an unsafe clique is unconcentrated in at most one R_i. Empty/singleton cliques cause no failure.

claims.name: All correspondences meet at F and all original cores at Id
claims.statement: Every R_i contains F. If intersection_i R_i had infinite classes it would contain a minimal infinite E_j, contrary to E_j meet R_j finite. Hence that intersection is F. The exact meet of C_i=kappa(R_i) lies in F and equals Id by normalization. The E_i list must be exhaustive.

claims.name: Original cores contain every other minimal direction
claims.statement: For j!=i, E_j<=R_i and E_j=kappa(E_j) by I09, so monotonicity gives E_j<=C_i. Thus C_i is infinite nonidentity for r>=2; E_i meet C_i=Id by C06/normalization. Each Q_i is actual, infinite and strictly smaller.

claims.name: Correspondence has one least strict coarsening
claims.statement: If an invariant D>R_i contains an atom a outside R_i, E_i meet a squared!=Id. If E_i meet D were proper in E_i it would have finite classes, contradicting C04. Therefore E_i<=D, so E_i join R_i is least above R_i. Its index over R_i is infinite by transposition and finite E_i meet R_i. Thus Sigma(R_i)=R_i.

claims.name: Original quotient finite bottom and upper interval
claims.statement: Packet finite index gives Sigma(C_i)=Sigma(R_i)=R_i. C35 identifies the FULL invariant quotient interval, so F_i=R_i/C_i is exactly the greatest finite-class equivalence of Q_i and has one least strict coarsening. No normalization of the old-core quotient is asserted.

claims.name: A meet-irreducible finite bottom has one minimal infinite direction
claims.statement: Under A10 let D be least above finite F. Each minimal infinite U has D<=U join F and [U join F:U] finite. Then D meet U is infinite, forcing U<=D and D=U join F. Distinct such U,V would have finite meet but [U:U meet V]=[U join V:V] finite since U join V<=V join F=D, contradiction.

claims.name: Canonical old-core unary targets and clique projections
claims.statement: Instantiate C19 with C18 and reuse I06 for acl_(Q_i)(A)=F_i[A]. C14 gives that every unsafe clique has all but at most one projection in a single finite F_j packet, conditional on the separate A05 palette input. These are the actual source canonical-coordinate conclusions.

claims.name: Actual exact quotient images of algebraic real points are algebraic
claims.statement: If t=pi_E(x) has infinite full Aut(T/pi_E A) orbit, each finite owner motion fixing pi_E A can be joined to identity on A by I03, and I02 lifts it fixing A. The resulting x images have infinitely many distinct E-owners. Contrapositive gives pi_E(acl_M A) subset acl_T(pi_E A). No global group section.

claims.name: Finite common kernel recovers real algebraicity from coordinates
claims.statement: If every pi_i(x) is algebraic over pi_i(A), its orbit under Aut(M/A) has only finitely many possible coordinate tuples. Each actual tuple fibre is one finite K-class, so the original orbit is finite. This uses no ambient CRT surjectivity or compatibility assumption.

claims.name: General finite-meet real closure pullback
claims.statement: Apply C21 separately to all actual K_i for the forward inclusion and C22 for the reverse. Thus acl_M(A)=intersection_i pi_i^{-1}(acl_(M/K_i)(pi_i A)). Empty families, when allowed, force M finite by finite-class Top and satisfy the same formula.

claims.name: Full inverse-image intersection is finite
claims.statement: The simultaneous map to product_i D_i has finite image on W, and each fibre is one finite K-class. Therefore W is finite, without onto marginal projections or full compatible tuples.

claims.name: That intersection is absolutely acl-closed
claims.statement: For x in acl_M(W), C21 sends every pi_i(x) into acl(pi_i W) subset acl(D_i)=D_i. Thus x is in every inverse image and in W. Reverse inclusion is tautological. Source asks W nonempty; no closure of a common owner is needed.

claims.name: Full complementary rectangle inherits absolute closure
claims.statement: For C meet K=Id, actual I11/I12 CRT identifies D times_B P with pi_C^{-1}(D) intersect pi_K^{-1}(P). C24/C25 give finite absolute closure. Both factors are absolutely closed; B is arbitrary finite nonempty with the stated onto images and need not itself be closed or harmless.

claims.name: Mixed rectangle orbit identity remains a separate interface
claims.statement: For every old atom a, original commutation gives C;a;K=(C join K);a;(C join K). Reuse I13; this is not an additional assumption for the independent C25 closure proof.

claims.name: Choose one minimal direction for all added owner names
claims.statement: If x is not algebraic over real A, its canonical intersection J_A=meet_a Gamma(col(x,a)) has infinite classes (else its class defines a finite A-set). Choose one minimal infinite E<=J_A. If every named owner kernel contains ALL minimal infinite directions, this SAME E lies below all of them.

claims.name: Good actual representatives avoid only finite bad fibres
claims.statement: In an infinite E-class inside each named owner class, each bad colour p contributes at most one finite F-class of neighbours of x. There are finitely many colours. Choose b_j outside that finite union AND outside {x}; its genuine diversity colour p_j is good, forcing E<=Gamma(p_j) by minimality.

claims.name: Harmlessness for every finite collection of owner sorts
claims.statement: The chosen E-class through x lies in all Gamma spoke classes for A and the b_j, making their intersection infinite. I05 prevents x being algebraic over those real representatives. Since their owner classes are definable from them, x is not algebraic over A and the added owner imaginaries. Handles empty A and zero owner names separately.

claims.name: Missing one minimal direction creates new real algebraicity
claims.statement: If E is minimal infinite and E not<=H, E meet H has finite classes. Choose x E u but not x F u. The finite nonempty set E[u] intersect H[x] makes x algebraic over u and the one owner H[x], while I06 gives acl(u)=F[u], excluding x.

claims.name: Full harmless-owner iff criterion
claims.statement: Combine C30 and C31: a full invariant owner kernel is harmless iff it contains EVERY minimal infinite direction, simultaneously for finite collections of sorts. This branch does not assume finite-exact normalization, exactness of those owner kernels, or a strong safe palette.

claims.name: Old-core closure bands
claims.statement: For r>=2 the cores meet Id by C15 and their quotient finite bottoms are C18. C19/I06 give unary closure without using unsafe-clique premises; substitute into C23. The inverse image of F_i[pi_i A] is exactly R_i[A], giving the source closure-band formula.

claims.name: Finite diagnostics do not certify source geometry
claims.statement: Rook, finite actual quotient/action and Cartesian-phase pair-table controls test the named interfaces; they do not prove CCO, infinite-orbit avoidance, real acl, all exactness or EPPA for arbitrary sources.

claims.name: Canonical quotients transport the FULL invariant interval
claims.statement: For A11, old G and full Aut of the complete named quotient have the SAME pair orbitals: old G is transitive inside each named orbit and full Aut preserves its name. Thus full invariant equivalences are exactly old-G invariant equivalences, bijecting with the original interval above K via pullback; finite relative indices are literal class counts. No global lifting of full quotient automorphisms follows.
